newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker queries Greenspan on check clearing.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker queries Greenspan on check clearing.

text.p: A member of the House banking committee asked Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in a letter sent Monday to prove the Fed did not subsidise check clearing for the past three years.

"I would appreciate your cooperation in sending me the 1995, 1996 and 1997 monthly reports from the ITS (Interdistrict Transportation System) on cost/revenue matching prepared at the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston," Carolyn Maloney, D-N.Y., said in the letter.
The Monetary Control Act of 1980 requires the Fed to recover all costs tied to the financial services it provides to the banking sector and the public, such as check clearing services.

Maloney, who queried Greenspan on the issue when he testified before Congress last month, has sponsored a bill to prevent the Fed from subsidising the specific stand-alone cost of transporting the estimated 25 billion checks the central bank clears every year.
Greenspan said during his regular Humphrey-Hawkins testimony that "for check services, as a group... (the Fed has) significant profits."
